links.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy and conversation length under simulated patient communication noise versus clean cases
links.effect: Realistic noise reduced diagnostic accuracy by 15-25 percentage points and increased conversation length by 34-55%; 7-8B models degraded 1.4x more than 70B+ models.
links.quote: Across seven open-weight LLMs, realistic noise reduces diagnostic accuracy by 15-25 percentage points and increases conversation length by 34-55%; the 7-8B models degrade 1.4x more than 70B+ models.

unlisted_practices: Patient simulation framework with controllable communication noise and UMLS-grounded claim verifier to preserve truth adherence
LLM-as-judge evaluation validated against physician and nurse ratings

screen.reason: The study develops and evaluates VeriSim, a patient simulation framework to stress-test clinical LLMs against realistic patient communication noise, measuring degradation in diagnostic accuracy.

primary.practice: stress-testing medical AI under noisy simulated patient communication
